name: South/North Course
description: Starting on the South Nine, finishing on the North Nine. The original championship layout.

name: North/East Course
description: Starting on the North Nine, finishing on the East Nine.

name: East/South Course
description: Starting on the East Nine, finishing on the South Nine.

name: West Course
description: Ranked No. 1 in Australia and consistently in World Top 10. Features dramatic undulations, bold bunkering, native grasses framing each hole, and beautifully contoured greens. Designed by Dr. Alister MacKenzie.

name: East Course
description: World Top 100 course complementing the West with superb bunkering and smaller, beautifully constructed greens. Designed by Alex Russell.

name: Kingston Heath
description: Consistently ranked in top 3 courses in Australia and top 20 in the world. Features superb conditioning, incomparable MacKenzie bunkering, and unique 19th hole.

name: Metropolitan
description: One of the finest championship courses in Australia. Greg Norman called the fairways the best he had played anywhere in the world.

name: Victoria
description: Consistently ranked among Australia's best. Features lightning-fast greens and some of the best bunkering in Australia. Home course of Peter Thomson.

name: North Course
description: Sandbelt course featuring excellent variety with elevation changes, irregular greens, heathland vegetation. Ranked among Australia's Top 10.

name: South Course
description: Longer, flatter than North with stunning views. Creek lines and dry stone walls characterize the layout.

name: Yarra Yarra
description: Melbourne Sandbelt course with distinct shift between intimate front nine and roomier back nine. Large, fast, undulating greens. Restored by Tom Doak in 2017.

name: Woodlands
description: Often called Melbourne's most underrated course. Known for pure bent grass greens, strategic bunkering, excellent one-shotters.

name: Barwon Heads
description: Classic links course on Bellarine Peninsula. Bouncy, firm and fast links turf with windswept greens. Crowned Best Golf Town in Australia.

name: The Dunes Course
description: Victoria's #1 public access course. Authentic links golf with dramatic dune formations. Nick Faldo praised Hole 13; Tom Watson called Hole 17 exquisite.

name: Old Course
description: True test of golf with strategic ball positioning essential. Features large tiered greens, coastal views, extreme elevation changes.

name: Moonah Course
description: Built in spirit of traditional links on former cattle ranching land. Features rolling terrain, dramatic bunkering, Bass Strait views. Designed by Greg Norman.

name: Gunnamatta Course
description: Situated near Gunnamatta Beach, embracing natural cup and bowl undulations. Generous fairway width with imaginative green shapes. Designed by Tom Doak.

name: Open Course
description: Only course in Australia designed specifically to host Australian Open. Stadium layout with spectator viewing platforms. Designed by Peter Thomson.

name: Legends Course
description: More forgiving than Open Course, weaving through mature Moonah trees. Each hole named after a golfing legend. Designed by Ross Perrett and Peter Thomson.

name: Beach Course
description: Links style course with arguably the best collection of Par 3s in Australia. Host of Victorian Open. Designed by Tony Cashmore.

name: Creek Course
description: Parkland layout regularly compared to Melbourne's best Sandbelt courses. Co-designed by Nick Faldo.

name: St Andrews Beach
description: Tom Doak's first Australian mainland design. #1 public access course on Australian mainland. Includes Australia's longest par-4.
